Kimberly / Jonas / Jordan —

Forwarding the thread with Nebula. They countered to 25% immediate, then 30/45-day splits. They asked for explicit confirmation that we will not suspend service while the tranches are honored.

My suggested options (pros/cons in attached spreadsheet):
1) Accept 25/30/45 tranche + binding DocuSign payment plan; commit to no-service-suspension while payments are received on schedule. Pro: fastest recovery, keeps customer happy. Con: extends exposure for 45 days on a EUR 178k receivable.
2) Accept 35/40/25 as I originally proposed, require VAT allocation evidence within 14 days, escalate to formal dunning (service suspension) if no evidence/late payment. Pro: stricter and reduces exposure. Con: higher probability of pushing them to pause.
3) Reject staged remit, initiate Stage 2 dunning now (7-day legal notice then service suspension). Pro: strongest collection posture. Con: risk to relationship and potential churn.

Given Nebula's strategic value and the AP note about a temporary operational delay, my recommendation is option 1 with a hard DocuSign plan and internal SLA: if any tranche misses by >3 business days without written notice, automatic escalation to Stage 2. I have attached a proposed dunning schedule and the short DocuSign payment plan text.

Requesting Kimberly's sign-off for option selection and Jordan to provide the service-suspension copy we would use in a follow-up if needed. Jonas — please flag any tax/VAT concerns (entity split / reverse-charge).

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — good write-up. I agree with a pragmatic path: take the payments and preserve the relationship with a clear, enforceable DocuSign payment plan. A couple of clarifications before we finalize:

- Legal: we need the DocuSign text to include an automatic escalation clause that triggers after a missed tranche (3 business days grace) and confirms Redwood's right to suspend access to paid features. Jordan, can you draft the exact suspension notice copy?
- Tax: Jonas, verify whether Nebula's VAT allocation requires re-billing to a different Redwood entity or if a supplier statement will suffice; if re-billing is required that might delay collection.
- CEO touchpoint: Given the account size, I concur we should not loop the CEO yet — keep escalation to CRO/CFO only unless we miss the initial tranche.

Hannah: prepare the DocuSign with (a) 25% immediate, (b) 30% in 30 days, (c) 45% in 45 days, include the VAT checklist (see attached short checklist I pulled from our tax playbook), and schedule an internal 15-minute alignment with Jordan and Legal (calendar invite).
